name: Soap
description:
A firm bar of plain household soap with a mild, clean scent. It is useful for washing hands, clothing and ordinary cooking utensils when water is available.

One bar is supplied without a box or washcloth. Track gradual wear manually; soap has no automatic effect on disease, poison or magical contamination.

weight.notes: Quarter-pound bar, substantial enough for repeated everyday use.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Needle
description:
A fine steel needle with a small eye, suited to ordinary cloth repairs and attaching buttons. It is sold in a folded scrap of paper to keep its point covered.

Thread, scissors and replacement cloth are separate purchases. The needle is a domestic sewing implement, not a set of thieves' tools or medical equipment.

weight.notes: Two thousandths of a pound per needle, preserving a small positive mass rather than treating bulk needles as weightless.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Thread
description:
A small wooden spool wound with 50 feet of plain linen sewing thread. It suits mending seams, replacing buttons and other light cloth repairs.

The price and weight cover the entire spool and thread. Partial use is tracked manually. This fine thread is not suitable for lifting loads or supporting a climber.
saleUnit: One spool holding 50 feet of linen thread

weight.notes: Two hundredths of a pound for the full spool and its light wooden core.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Sewing Kit
description:
A folding cloth wallet containing two needles, 50 feet of linen thread, small scissors, a few plain buttons and modest cloth patches. It covers routine repairs to travel clothes and household linens.

All listed contents are included in the purchase weight. This is a small domestic kit, not a full set of weaver's tools, and it grants no tool proficiency or healing ability. Replacement thread, buttons and patches are bought separately as they are used.

weight.notes: Fifteen hundredths of a pound for the complete light kit, including its cloth wallet.

name: Broom
description:
A bundle of tightly bound straw fixed to a smooth wooden handle. It is a dependable broom for sweeping dust, dry leaves and crumbs from hard floors.

This is ordinary household equipment. It includes no dustpan and has no magical properties.

weight.notes: One and a half pounds for a full-length light wooden handle and bound straw head.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Mop
description:
Strips of absorbent cloth are secured to the end of a wooden handle for washing floors and wiping up spills. The head can be rinsed and wrung out by hand.

Sold dry, without soap or a bucket. A wet mop may be heavier while being carried; the listed weight is for the dry item.

weight.notes: One and a quarter pounds for the dry handle and cloth head. Retained water is not included.

name: Wash Bucket
description:
A light metal bucket with a rolled rim and swinging handle, intended for carrying wash water and cleaning supplies.

Sold empty. It holds up to 3 gallons or 24 lb of contents. The open top makes spills likely on a rough journey; there is no sealing lid. Water, soap and cloths are separate purchases, and any carried contents add their own weight.

weight.notes: One and a half pounds for the empty thin metal bucket and handle; a full water load adds up to 24 lb.

name: Wash Board
description:
A compact wooden board with a ridged working face and smooth handhold. Rubbing wet cloth against the ribs helps loosen ordinary dirt during washing.

The board is supplied without a tub, bucket or soap. It is a household aid and has no special effect on stains or substances that require unusual treatment.

weight.notes: Two pounds for a sturdy wooden board sized for use over a basin or small tub.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Clothes Line
description:
A 50-foot length of tightly twisted light cord for hanging washing between posts or trees. It coils into a small bundle when the laundry is taken down.

Pegs and supports are not included. This cord is made for clothing and light household loads, not climbing, lifting people or replacing full-strength hempen rope.

weight.notes: One pound for fifty feet of light laundry cord, substantially lighter than climbing rope.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Cloth Rags
description:
Six clean offcuts of plain cloth wipe tools, polish dry surfaces or soak up small spills. The pieces are assorted shapes but large enough to fold around a hand.

They are domestic cleaning supplies, not sterile dressings or a healer's kit. Washing, drying and replacing worn pieces are ordinary household work.
saleUnit: One tied bundle of six clean cloth rags

weight.notes: A quarter pound for six light cloth pieces and their tie.

name: Hand Towel
description:
A hemmed rectangle of absorbent linen dries hands, dishes or small cleaned objects. A sewn loop allows it to hang near a wash place.

The towel is supplied dry and clean. It has no cleansing or medical effect of its own; soap and wash water are separate.
saleUnit: One linen hand towel, two by one foot

weight.notes: One fifth of a pound for a single small hemmed linen towel.

name: Clothes Pegs
description:
Twelve split hardwood pegs pin light washing to a clothes line. Their tapered slots grip the fabric and cord without separate metal springs.

The line and washing are separate. Strong wind or a heavy wet blanket can still pull a poorly fitted peg loose.
saleUnit: One set of twelve split wooden clothes pegs

weight.notes: Fifteen hundredths of a pound for twelve small pegs.

name: Wooden Buttons
description:
Twelve plain two-hole wooden buttons repair everyday shirts, wraps and cloth bags. Their rounded edges are smoothed to reduce snagging.

A needle and thread are separate. The packet contains fastening pieces rather than a complete garment or a set of metal armour fittings.
saleUnit: One packet of twelve plain wooden buttons

weight.notes: Three hundredths of a pound for twelve small wooden buttons and a paper fold.

name: Thimble
description:
A dimpled brass cap protects a fingertip while pushing a sewing needle through ordinary fabric. Its shallow open rim fits one adult finger.

Needles and thread are separate. It is a mending aid rather than a proficiency tool set, protective armour or a means of handling dangerous substances.

weight.notes: Two hundredths of a pound for a thin brass finger cap.

name: Comb
description:
A small polished bone comb has coarse teeth at one end and finer teeth at the other. It loosens ordinary tangles and helps keep hair tidy.

This is personal grooming equipment, distinct from the horse's metal Curry Comb. It removes no condition or infestation automatically.

weight.notes: Five hundredths of a pound for one small polished bone comb.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Door Hinges
description:
Two plain iron strap hinges and twelve fitting nails suit a small wooden door, shutter or sturdy box lid. Their broad leaves spread the load over the timber.

A hammer, door and latch are separate. Suitability depends on the timber and fitting; the hinges do not themselves secure or lock an opening.
saleUnit: One pair of small iron strap hinges with twelve nails

weight.notes: One pound for both small hinges, pins and their fitting nails.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Padlock
description:
An iron padlock closes through a suitable hasp or pair of chain links. One fitted key is supplied; a spare key or fitting a door hasp is separate work.

Use the 2014 ordinary-lock benchmark: a creature proficient with thieves' tools can pick it with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Apply that check manually; it is not proof against breaking its mounting.
saleUnit: One ordinary iron padlock with one key

weight.notes: Half a pound for the small lock and its included key.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Mortar and Pestle
description:
A shallow stone bowl and rounded hand pestle crush dry herbs, spice seeds and similar kitchen ingredients. The rough working surfaces help break pieces down under steady pressure.

Ingredients are separate. This is ordinary preparation equipment, not an alchemist's proficiency set and not a device that creates potions or identifies substances.
saleUnit: One small stone mortar with matching pestle

weight.notes: Two pounds for the small bowl and matching pestle, with no ingredients included.
